To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
confidence in decision is affected by response uncertainty in a manner similar to the effect of ‘known information’ on decision time.

(1) confidence in decision was significantly reduced when the response was uncertain; (2) confidence in decision increased as the amount of ‘known information’ increased; and (3) confidence in decision decreased as the amount of unknown information increased.

(1) confidence in decision is a function of response uncertainty, amount of information, and their interaction, and (2) response uncertainty and amount information have different effects on confidence in decision and on decision time.

the relationship between the amount of information and the amount of response uncertainty and their effects on the subjective uncertainty of the decision maker.
the effects of response uncertainty, ‘known information,’ and ‘unknown information’ on confidence in decision and on decision time.
the relationship of subjective uncertainty to response uncertainty and amount and degree of information.
